headline: China's technology ministry has reportedly approved Alibaba's Qwen AI models for use in Apple's iPhones, including the new iPhone Duo.
score_reason: Kept at pool score: regulatory clearance affecting a huge market, but single-origin report.
importance_line: Millions of iPhone users in China could soon get Apple's AI features running on Alibaba's models, which matters to Apple, Alibaba and rivals, though the only source is an Alibaba-owned newspaper and Apple has not commented.
summary: The South China Morning Post, which Engadget notes is owned by Alibaba, reports that the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology has cleared Alibaba's Qwen language models and its Wanxiang image and video tool for Apple handsets, with the iPhone Duo due to launch in China next week. Apple won clearance for Apple Intelligence in mainland China in July but has not yet launched it there, and has not said what it plans.
notes: SCMP page blocked; text read via Engadget and Computerworld. Category POL (government approval, geopolitics).
